content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text does the governed thing by using Matthew 1:16's admission of both readings as the ground for UNDERDETERMINED.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. It is not, if the judge names another verse or phrase that settles it.","room":"never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED — I weighed whether the judge's references to the parties' answers count as naming another verse or phrase that settles it, or whether the rule requires a specific settling verse or phrase; I read it as the latter.","why":"The judge rests UNDERDETERMINED on Matthew 1:16 admitting both readings and only refers to round sections, not a named settling verse or phrase, so it breaches K-S2."}
